newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: U.S. UPSETS AUSTRALIAN DEBT MARKET ONCE AGAIN.
newsitem.headline: U.S. UPSETS AUSTRALIAN DEBT MARKET ONCE AGAIN.

text.p: *Long dated Australian bond yields rose sharply in early trading as U.S. Treasuries came under renewed pressure in the wake of the U.S. 30-year bond quarterly refunding auction.
*Local housing finance data due at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT).
Long dated Australian bond yields rose sharply in early trading as U.S. Treasuries came under renewed pressure in the wake of the U.S. 30-year bond quarterly refunding auction.

The final auction in the refunding series went off reasonably well at a yield of 6.445 percent, but a lack of retail demand forced dealers to cheapen up the issue and the yield ended the day at 6.50 percent.
The outstanding 30-year bond yield ended five basis points higher at 6.53 percent, its first time above 6.50 percent since July 21.

The U.S. move put support at 93.470 on the local September 10-year bond futures contract under severe pressure, although analysts said as long as the contract goes into the weekend above 93.400 the market's recent uptrend remains intact.

The contract had touched a high of 93.600 at one stage in after hours trading, regaining its composure after an initial negative response to Thursday's labour force data which contained an unexpected jump in full-employment.
"The market regathered its strength after forming a view that the present setting in monetary policy will remain for a considerable period of time," ANZ analysts said in a report.
The local market's initial weak tone saw an underperforming bias against U.S. and Canadian debt. However, the negative spread against New Zealand continued to widen as the N.Z. dollar slid again.
